gaps.sentence: There isn't ___ room in here for a piano.
gaps.explanation: 'Enough room' means sufficient space; the negative 'isn't' shows the space is insufficient.

gaps.sentence: Hardly ___ came to the afternoon lecture.
gaps.explanation: 'Hardly anyone' is already negative — do not add 'no one'.

gaps.sentence: This suitcase is ___ heavy to carry.
gaps.hint: adjective + this word + to-infinitive = impossible result
gaps.explanation: 'Too heavy to carry' means it is more heavy than possible; 'very' and 'so' cannot be followed directly by 'to'.

gaps.sentence: ___ money was spent on advertising last year.
There is so ___ crime in this area that people are afraid.
gaps.explanation: 'So much' is used with uncountable nouns like crime; 'plenty' would need 'of'.

gaps.sentence: Every one of the switches ___ been tested twice.
gaps.explanation: 'Every one of' takes a singular verb: has.

gaps.sentence: ___ of my two brothers work in banking.
gaps.explanation: 'Both of my two brothers work ...' is correct; 'all' and 'none' are not used for two.

gaps.sentence: The ___ of teenagers own a smartphone these days.
gaps.explanation: 'The majority of + plural noun' means most of them; 'the number of teenagers own' would be ungrammatical.
